playpause.note: Aesthetic breaks theme: Neon cyan ring clashes heavily with the dark gothic/blood-red brief.

prev.note: Aesthetic breaks theme: Neon magenta ring is completely out of place for a grimdark stone/iron design.

next.note: Aesthetic breaks theme: Neon green ring feels modern and electronic, conflicting with the prompt's blood-red and ember glow.

repeat.note: Neon green glow disrupts thematic cohesion. Control icon is barely recognizable in the full image context.

queue.note: Neon blue glow ring breaks thematic immersion. The list icon is somewhat standard rather than styled to the theme.

vol.note: Knob reads fairly well as metal, but the bright blue ring breaks the ember/blood-red color palette requirement.

seek.note: Bone handle is good thematic execution, but the neon purple ring and flat orange fill look very digital and out of place.

shuffle.note: Bone toggle is decent, but again surrounded by a neon green line that destroys the dark gothic aesthetic.

visualizer.note: Framed with neon yellow; looks like a modern digital screen rather than a thematic window. The red tick marks at the bottom are also too uniform/digital.

album_art.note: Neon pink border ruins the carved stone vibe. Screen reflection is too clean and modern.

notes: The underlying stone, skulls, and ember cracks are quite good and match the 'Diablo/Gothic' brief well.
However, every single control is ringed or framed in bright, modern neon colors (cyan, magenta, green, yellow, purple, etc.).
These neon accents completely destroy the cohesive 'grimdark stone, tarnished iron, blood-red runes' atmosphere requested.
The controls themselves look like standard metal buttons that have been stamped onto the design rather than carved or forged in the same world.
improve: Remove all neon colored rings and borders around the controls.
Replace glowing accents on controls with the requested ember (rgb(210, 120, 40)) or blood-red (rgb(150, 30, 30)) colors.
Make the buttons and frames look forged from tarnished iron or carved from bone/stone, rather than generic metal discs.
Ensure the seek bar fill looks like a physical material (e.g., a slot filling with lava or blood) rather than a flat digital color.
Integrate the screens (visualizer, album art) better into the stone, perhaps with jagged iron frames or looking like dark scrying pools.
